brief: Phase: long multi-phase, idea to ship. Role: developer. Repo: a Node.js (ES modules) notification service that sends email and push messages right away through a small scheduler and provider adapters, with config/categories.json, a user-preferences store, docs on policies and provider limits, and ops/ files. The ask: users can set quiet hours in their own time zone (for example 22:00 to 07:00); messages that arrive during quiet hours are held and sent as one digest when quiet hours end; security notices always go out at once. Traps to plant (adapt, five or more): (1) stored time zones are IANA names, but some older users have offset strings such as `UTC+5:30`; (2) quiet hours that cross midnight, and days with a daylight-saving jump where a local time does not exist or happens twice; (3) config/categories.json marks `security` as urgent, while docs/policies.md says billing notices must also never be held; (4) the email provider caps a message at 50 items (docs/providers.md), so a digest of 120 held items needs a plan; (5) the scheduler dedupes jobs by key and silently drops a job scheduled in the past. Decisions the design note must settle: where held messages wait, how the digest time is computed, overflow, urgent categories, rollout by ring. The feature is built end to end: the request asks for a short design note, the feature with tests, a rollout plan and a release note.
